campaign.title: Violet Sorrengail's Tale
campaign.synopsis: It's finally Conscription Day. Violet Sorrengail, an aspiring apprentice scribe, is currently struggling carrying her bag filled with books

world.genreTone: Dark Military Fantasy, High-Stakes, Romance, and Grim Realism
world.conflict: The brutal, high-mortality training at Basgiath War College, set against Navarre's desperate, secret war against the venin and their wyvern forces, while the leadership actively censors the truth from its own citizens.
world.powerSystem: Signet powers channeled through bonded dragons from the sky, paired with physical combat, runes, and the deadly, life-draining magic of the dark-channeling venin.
world.eraTechLevel: Pseudo-Medieval / Early Renaissance with localized magical advancements, featuring massive stone fortresses, swords, crossbows, and armor, but lacking gunpowder.
world.keyFactions: The Riders Quadrant, the Scribes Quadrant, the Navarre Military Leadership (General Sorrengail's faction), and the secret revolution/Aretia survivors.
world.background: For four hundred years, Navarre has been protected by its magical wards, fueled by the dragons of the Basgiath mountains. While the Scribes rewrite history to hide the existence of the dark-magic-wielding venin and their flying wyvern, cadets at Basgiath War College are forced through a deadly curriculum where failure means death. With the wards beginning to fail and the truth leaking to the edges of the kingdom, the college has become a pressure cooker of political tension, lethal training, and forbidden knowledge.
world.narrationStyle: Third person, close POV on the protagonist, grounded and cinematic.
world.sourceScope: Book 1 (Fourth Wing) only, through the ending

player.name: Violet Sorrengail
player.background: Trained her entire life by her father to become a Scribe, Violet has spent her years surrounded by books, history, and quiet archives. She suffers from a chronic, unnamed connective tissue condition that makes her joints easily dislocate and her bones brittle, rendering her physically fragile in a world that values raw strength. Her mother, the cold and formidable General Lilith Sorrengail, has suddenly decreed that Violet will not enter the safety of the Scribe Quadrant, but must instead face Conscription Day for the lethal Riders Quadrant, just as her siblings Mira and the late Brennan did.
player.personality: Quietly stubborn, highly analytical, and fiercely resilient. Violet possesses a sharp, brilliant mind that weaponizes historical knowledge and tactical observation to compensate for her physical limitations. She is deeply loyal, possesses a quiet courage, and refuses to let her physical fragility define her capability.
player.motivation: To survive the brutal, high-mortality training of the Riders Quadrant without letting her physical limitations get her killed, while desperately trying to prove she belongs in this world on her own terms despite her mother's harsh mandate.
player.physicalTrait: Slight of build, with pale skin and distinctive hair that starts dark brown but fades to a metallic silver-white at the ends. She possesses fragile joints wrapped in protective bindings and a delicate stature that contrasts sharply with the armored cadets around her.
player.secret: She carries a deep, forbidden knowledge of Navarian history and military tactics passed down from her late father—information that the Scribe Quadrant actively censors and that could make her a target if she speaks it aloud.

the_parapet.name: The Parapet
the_parapet.description: A terrifyingly narrow, slick stone bridge suspended hundreds of feet in the air, connecting the outer wall to the Riders Quadrant. It is the lethal first test of Conscription Day, where wind, rain, and vertigo claim their first victims.

riders_quadrant.name: Riders Quadrant
riders_quadrant.description: The brutal heart of Basgiath's combat forces. Built around a massive stone courtyard, this is where cadets train, sleep, and constantly fight for survival under the watchful eyes of their flight leaders.

scribes_quadrant.name: Scribes Quadrant
scribes_quadrant.description: A vast, silent labyrinth of endless bookshelves, quiet study carrels, and subterranean archives. It is a sanctuary of knowledge, but also the engine of Navarre's systematic censorship.

the_gauntlet.name: The Gauntlet
the_gauntlet.description: A deadly, mechanical obstacle course built into a sheer cliffside. Cadets must navigate spinning logs, swinging blades, and vertical climbs under extreme time pressure to prove they are agile enough to mount a dragon.

the_flight_field.name: The Flight Field & Bowl
the_flight_field.description: The massive, open-air valley and stone amphitheater where dragons and riders meet. It is here that Threshing takes place, and where bonded cadets learn the terrifying, exhilarating art of flight.

athebyne.name: Athebyne
athebyne.description: An isolated, sun-bleached military outpost on the southern border of Navarre. Situated at the very edge of the magical wards, it is a desolate place of dry heat, strategic tension, and hidden truths.

basgiath_war_college.name: Basgiath War College
basgiath_war_college.description: A colossal, ancient stone fortress carved directly into the rugged peaks of the Blackwood Mountains. It is divided into distinct, highly competitive quadrants, designed to forge the defenders of Navarre or kill them in the attempt.

the_outskirts.name: The Outskirts & Borders
the_outskirts.description: The treacherous mountainous terrain surrounding the college and the wider, ward-protected kingdom of Navarre, where the illusion of safety begins to wear thin.

mira_sorrengail.name: Mira Sorrengail
mira_sorrengail.role: Rider Lieutenant and Protective Older Sister
mira_sorrengail.personality: Fierce, fiercely loyal, pragmatic, and highly capable
mira_sorrengail.appearance: Athletic and muscular, with short-cropped hair, wearing scale-armor and carrying her signature dragon-scaled daggers

xaden_riorson.name: Xaden Riorson
xaden_riorson.personality: Brooding, lethal, intensely observant, and carrying a heavy burden of responsibility
xaden_riorson.appearance: Tall, strikingly handsome, with dark hair, golden-flecked eyes, and a jagged scar running down his jawline

dain_aetos.name: Dain Aetos
dain_aetos.role: Second-Year Squad Leader and Childhood Friend
dain_aetos.personality: Rule-abiding, protective to a fault, traditional, and deeply structured
dain_aetos.appearance: Clean-cut, handsome, wearing the neat uniform of a second-year rider, with a earnest but often anxious expression

lilith_sorrengail.name: General Lilith Sorrengail
lilith_sorrengail.role: Commanding General of Navarre and Violet's Mother
lilith_sorrengail.personality: Cold, uncompromising, fiercely demanding, and emotionally distant
lilith_sorrengail.appearance: Imposing and austere, with dark hair tightly bound, wearing the pristine, decorated uniform of the Navarrian high command

tairn.name: Tairnageon
tairn.personality: Arrogant, ancient, intensely proud, and fiercely protective of his chosen rider
tairn.appearance: A massive, terrifying black dragon with huge wings, gold eyes, and a clubbed tail capable of crushing stone

discovery.teaser: A massive shadow looms over the Flight Field, a creature of ancient power who refuses to bond with the weak—yet whose gaze seems to linger on you.

navarre_military_leadership.name: Navarre Military Leadership
navarre_military_leadership.description: Led by General Lilith Sorrengail and Colonel Aethelgard, this faction prioritizes the defense of Navarre's borders at all costs. They enforce the brutal, high-mortality training of Basgiath War College and systematically censor any information regarding the fading wards or the existence of venin to maintain absolute control over the populace.

riders_quadrant_leadership.name: Riders Quadrant Leadership
riders_quadrant_leadership.description: Consisting of ruthless instructors, wingleaders, and section leaders like Varrish and Dain Aetos. They believe only the strongest deserve to bond dragons and survive. They enforce a strict, lethal hierarchy where weakness is a death sentence, and they view Violet's physical fragility as an insult to the quadrant's legacy.

griffin_flyers_of_poromiel.name: Griffin Flyers of Poromiel
griffin_flyers_of_poromiel.description: The military forces of Navarre's neighboring rival, Poromiel. Riding fierce, winged griffins, these flyers launch desperate raids along the border. They are viewed by Navarian citizens as bloodthirsty invaders, but they are actually fighting a desperate, losing battle against a dark threat that Navarre refuses to acknowledge.

the_revolutionaries.name: The Revolutionaries
the_revolutionaries.description: A clandestine network of rebels, many of whom are the children of executed separatists bearing rebellion relics. Led in secret by Xaden Riorson, they smuggle weapons and dragon-matured alloy across the borders to help those outside Navarre's wards defend themselves against the venin.

discovery.teaser: Whispers of treason circulate among the marked children of the rebellion, who share silent glances and carry secrets that could get them executed by the leadership.

dragon_rider_bond.name: The Dragon-Rider Bond
dragon_rider_bond.content: A sacred, telepathic connection forged during Threshing. Dragons do not choose riders out of pity; they choose strength, honor, and survival. Once bonded, a dragon channels raw magic into their rider, which manifests as a unique 'signet' power tailored to the rider's personality and soul. However, this bond is a double-edged sword: if a dragon dies, the shock can kill the rider; if a rider dies, the dragon suffers immensely, though they may survive to bond again. No rider can bond more than one dragon, and dragons never bond more than one rider at a time—with exceedingly rare, historic exceptions.

culling_traditions.name: The Culling of Basgiath
culling_traditions.content: The Riders Quadrant operates on a brutal philosophy of forced natural selection. From the moment cadets step onto the Parapet, they are subjected to lethal trials where failure means death. Murder among cadets is not only permitted but expected, provided it occurs outside of formal classes and before the presentation of dragons. The leadership believes that a high mortality rate during training ensures only the most ruthless, physically dominant, and tactically brilliant cadets survive to bond dragons, weeded out before they can weaken the sky-bound defense forces of Navarre.

navarre_poromiel_conflict.name: The Border War of Navarre and Poromiel
navarre_poromiel_conflict.content: For four centuries, the kingdom of Navarre has maintained a bitter border war with the neighboring nation of Poromiel. Protected by magical wards fueled by Navarre's unique dragon species, Navarian citizens live in relative safety. Poromiel, a land of open plains lacking these natural mountain defenses, relies on griffin riders to patrol their borders. Officially, the conflict is fought over resources and trade routes, with Navarre portraying the griffin flyers as desperate, aggressive raiders trying to breach the protective wards.

the_venin_threat.name: The Great Censorship: Venin and Wyvern
the_venin_threat.content: The true nature of the war is systematically erased by the Scribe Quadrant. The griffin flyers of Poromiel are not raiding Navarre for plunder; they are desperately fighting for survival against venin—ancient, corrupted humans who draw magic directly from the earth rather than a bonded beast, draining the life from the soil to power themselves. These venin create and control wyvern, massive two-legged beasts that breathe fire through dark runes. Navarre's leadership actively hides this threat, letting neighboring provinces burn rather than extending the protection of their dragon-fueled wards beyond the national border.

discovery.teaser: A scorched, blood-stained page torn from an ancient history book, containing sketches of winged beasts with two legs instead of four, and a warning about the earth turning to ash.

beats.title: Chapter 1: The General's Mandate
beats.summary: Violet is summoned by her mother, General Lilith Sorrengail, who brutally shatters her dreams of becoming a Scribe, forcing her into the lethal Riders Quadrant.

beats.title: Chapter 2: The Deadly Crossing
beats.summary: Violet faces the terrifying, rain-slicked Parapet, surviving the crossing through her intelligence and the unexpected aid of her sister's customized armor.

beats.title: Chapter 3: Eyes of the Wingleader
beats.summary: Violet enters the quadrant and has her first hostile encounter with Xaden Riorson, the son of the executed rebel leader who has every reason to want her dead.

beats.title: Chapter 4: Sleepless and Marked
beats.summary: In the barracks, Violet meets her squadmates, navigates the immediate social hierarchy, and realizes just how many cadets want to murder her in her sleep.

beats.title: Chapter 5: The Sparring Ring
beats.summary: Combat training begins under the brutal direction of the wing leadership, forcing Violet to use daggers and poison to survive against physically superior opponents.

beats.title: Chapter 6: Whispers in the Scribe Archives
beats.summary: Violet sneaks into the Scribe Quadrant to seek comfort in books, only to realize her childhood friend Dain Aetos is deeply committed to the rules, even at her expense.

beats.title: Chapter 7: A Lesson in Mortality
beats.summary: A classmate is ruthlessly killed during a training exercise, cementing the reality that failure at Basgiath is punishable by immediate death.

beats.title: Chapter 8: Sizing Up the Obstacles
beats.summary: The physical Gauntlet is revealed; Violet realizes her hyper-flexible joints make the standard methods of climbing it physically impossible.

beats.title: Chapter 9: Brewing the Solution
beats.summary: With the help of Rhiannon, Violet brews poisons to coat her daggers, deciding to fight dirty to level the playing field against her brutal classmates.

beats.title: Chapter 10: Under the Wingleader's Watch
beats.summary: Xaden catches Violet training in the dark, initiating a tense, highly charged physical confrontation where he challenges her survival instincts.

beats.title: Chapter 11: Scaling the Impossible
beats.summary: Violet runs the Gauntlet, using her own unorthodox, agile methods to bypass the obstacles, earning the begrudging respect of her peers.

beats.title: Chapter 12: Facing the Dragons
beats.summary: The cadets are presented to the dragons in the Bowl, where the massive beasts inspect the candidates and incinerate those they deem unworthy.

beats.title: Chapter 13: Whispers of the Unbonded
beats.summary: On the eve of Threshing, tension spikes as unbonded cadets plot to murder weaker candidates like Violet to increase their own chances of bonding.

beats.title: Chapter 14: Into the Valley
beats.summary: Threshing begins in the valley; Violet must navigate the dangerous terrain while avoiding both hostile classmates and territorial dragons.

beats.title: Chapter 15: Standing Against the Pack
beats.summary: Violet discovers a group of cadets trying to assassinate a defenseless golden dragon, Andarna, and steps in to defend her at the risk of her own life.

beats.title: Chapter 16: Chosen by the Legends
beats.summary: In a shocking turn of events, Violet is bonded not only by the golden Andarna, but also by the massive, lethal Black Morningstartail, Tairn.

beats.title: Chapter 17: Shockwaves in the Quadrant
beats.summary: The college is in uproar over Violet's unprecedented double bond, forcing Xaden Riorson to take her under his direct wing as her flight instructor.

beats.title: Chapter 18: Finding a Grip
beats.summary: Violet struggles to stay on Tairn's massive back during flight maneuvers, prompting a search for a solution before she falls to her death.

beats.title: Chapter 19: Bound to the Sky
beats.summary: Xaden presents Violet with a custom-designed saddle that accommodates her physical limitations, cementing their growing, complicated trust.

beats.title: Chapter 20: Channelling the Unseen
beats.summary: As the physical bond deepens, Violet begins to feel the raw, untamed magical energy of her dragons flowing into her, waiting to manifest as a signet.

beats.title: Chapter 21: Training the Tail
beats.summary: Violet's squad begins collective flight training, forcing her to coordinate with Dain and Rhiannon while keeping the secrets of Andarna's youth hidden.

beats.title: Chapter 22: Slashing in the Dark
beats.summary: Violet is attacked in her sleep by a group of rebellious unbonded cadets, forcing her to fight for her life using her daggers and raw agility.

beats.title: Chapter 23: Dain's Touch
beats.summary: Following the assassination attempt, Dain uses his memory-reading signet to investigate, forcing Violet to guard her thoughts about Xaden.

beats.title: Chapter 24: Manifesting the Storm
beats.summary: During a high-stress confrontation on the flight field, Violet's signet finally manifests as raw, devastating lightning, marking her as incredibly powerful.

beats.title: Chapter 25: Grounding the Spark
beats.summary: Violet must learn to control her volatile lightning signet before she accidentally destroys the college or burns her own nervous system out.

beats.title: Chapter 26: Midnight Negotiations
beats.summary: Violet discovers Xaden meeting secretly with other marked children of the rebellion, realizing there is a deeper conspiracy brewing within Basgiath.

beats.title: Chapter 27: Strategizing the Board
beats.summary: The annual War Games are announced; Violet uses her Scribe-trained mind to analyze historical battle patterns, spotting anomalies in Navarre's defense reports.

beats.title: Chapter 28: Scribes vs. Riders
beats.summary: A tense dispute between the Scribe Quadrant and the Riders Quadrant forces Violet to choose between her past academic life and her present military reality.

beats.title: Chapter 29: Igniting the Spark
beats.summary: Under the cover of a mountain storm, the simmering romantic and physical tension between Violet and Xaden finally boils over into a passionate encounter.

beats.title: Chapter 30: Broken Trust
beats.summary: Violet realizes that Dain has been using his signet on her without her permission, stealing her memories and feeding them to the high command.

beats.title: Chapter 31: Deployed to the Outposts
beats.summary: As part of the War Games, Violet's squad is suddenly deployed to the remote outpost of Athebyne, far from the safety of the magical wards.

beats.title: Chapter 32: The Desolation of Athebyne
beats.summary: Arriving at Athebyne, Violet and Xaden's wing find the outpost abandoned and stripped of its defenses, realizing they have been set up by leadership.

beats.title: Chapter 33: The Gryphon's Shadow
beats.summary: At Athebyne, Violet is confronted by Griffin Flyers from Poromiel, discovering that Xaden has been secretly supplying them with weapons.

beats.title: Chapter 34: The Real Enemy
beats.summary: Xaden reveals the ultimate secret: the venin and their wyvern are real, they are invading, and Navarre's leadership is actively letting the borders burn.

beats.title: Chapter 35: The Skies Burn
beats.summary: A swarm of venin and their terrifying wyvern launch a massive assault on the nearby village of Resson, forcing Violet to make a choice.

beats.title: Chapter 36: Standing Against the Dark
beats.summary: Violet and her allies engage in a desperate, bloody battle against the venin, using her lightning signet to strike down the flying beasts.

beats.title: Chapter 37: Poisoned Veins
beats.summary: Violet is mortally wounded by a venin's blade, her veins turning black as the dark magic begins to drain her life force while Xaden desperately flies her away.

beats.title: Chapter 38: Awakening in Aretia
beats.summary: Violet wakes up days later in the ruined, secretly rebuilt city of Aretia, saved by a mysterious mender who neutralized the venin poison.

beats.title: Chapter 39: The Ghost of the Past
beats.summary: Violet is reunited with her brother Brennan, long thought dead, and must face the reality that her entire life has been built on a web of deadly lies.

event_ch1_mira_parting.title: Mira's Warning
event_ch1_mira_parting.guidance: Ensure Mira gives Violet her scale armor and the crucial advice to trust no one, emphasizing that her physical fragility is her greatest target.

event_ch2_meyer_fall.title: The Fall of Jack's Victim
event_ch2_meyer_fall.guidance: Introduce Jack Barlowe early on the Parapet as he ruthlessly shoves another cadet to their death, establishing him as an immediate threat to Violet.

event_ch3_xaden_glance.title: The Eye of the Storm
event_ch3_xaden_glance.guidance: Describe the palpable, deadly tension when Xaden notices Violet's silver hair and realizes she is General Sorrengail's daughter.

event_ch4_dain_reunion.title: Dain's Overprotection
event_ch4_dain_reunion.guidance: Dain tries to convince Violet to transfer to the Scribes, expressing doubt in her survival and establishing his rule-abiding nature.

event_ch5_poison_choice.title: A Scribe's Arsenal
event_ch5_poison_choice.guidance: Highlight Violet's decision to use her knowledge of botany to create non-lethal muscle relaxants to coat her sparring daggers.

event_ch6_rhiannon_bond.title: Rhiannon's Boots
event_ch6_rhiannon_bond.guidance: Violet trades her high-quality boots to Rhiannon, cementing their loyalty and forming her first true friendship in the quadrant.

event_ch7_jack_threat.title: Jack's Promise
event_ch7_jack_threat.guidance: Jack Barlowe corners Violet in the corridor, promising to snap her neck the moment they are allowed to duel.

event_ch8_imogen_grudge.title: Imogen's Hostility
event_ch8_imogen_grudge.guidance: Imogen, a marked rebel child, displays open hostility toward Violet, pushing her hard during physical conditioning.

event_ch9_poisoning_the_ring.title: Levelling the Field
event_ch9_poisoning_the_ring.guidance: Violet successfully uses her poisoned daggers in a sparring match, proving that intellect can overcome raw physical strength.

event_ch10_xaden_lesson.title: Rooftop Sparring
event_ch10_xaden_lesson.guidance: Xaden forces Violet to defend herself on the castle battlements, teaching her how to use her low center of gravity to her advantage.

event_ch11_gauntlet_triumph.title: The Unorthodox Climb
event_ch11_gauntlet_triumph.guidance: Show Violet using her flexibility and a custom-engineered rope technique to scale the final wall of the Gauntlet, shocking the instructors.

event_ch12_dragon_terror.title: The Breath of Gold
event_ch12_dragon_terror.guidance: A cadet is incinerated by an orange dragon for showing fear, heightening the stakes right before Violet's eyes.

event_ch13_unbonded_plot.title: Whispers in the Dark
event_ch13_unbonded_plot.guidance: Violet overhears Jack Barlowe and his cronies planning to kill the golden feathertail dragon to prevent anyone weak from bonding it.

event_ch14_valley_hunt.title: The Hunted
event_ch14_valley_hunt.guidance: Violet is hunted through the rocky terrain of the valley by three unbonded cadets, forcing her to run toward the high ridges.

event_ch15_standing_ground.title: Defending Andarna
event_ch15_standing_ground.guidance: Violet uses her daggers and tactical positioning to fight off the attackers who are trying to kill the sleeping Andarna.

event_ch16_the_black_dragon.title: Tairn's Choice
event_ch16_the_black_dragon.guidance: Tairn lands with earth-shattering force, rejecting all other riders and demanding that Violet claim him alongside Andarna.

event_ch17_rebel_deal.title: The Wingleader's Duty
event_ch17_rebel_deal.guidance: Xaden is forced by the dragon elders to protect Violet, as Tairn is mated to Xaden's dragon, Sgaeyl; if Violet dies, Tairn dies, killing Sgaeyl.

event_ch18_the_slip.title: Nearly Falling
event_ch18_the_slip.guidance: During a steep dive, Violet slips from Tairn's back and is only saved by Tairn catching her mid-air with his massive claws.

event_ch19_the_gift.title: The Leather and Steel
event_ch19_the_gift.guidance: Xaden helps Violet strap into her new custom saddle, a moment of intense physical proximity and emotional vulnerability.

event_ch20_first_spark.title: Static in the Air
event_ch20_first_spark.guidance: Show static electricity jumping from Violet's fingers whenever she gets emotional or stands near Xaden.

event_ch21_andarnas_secret.title: The Golden Secret
event_ch21_andarnas_secret.guidance: Tairn warns Violet that Andarna's time-stopping ability must remain a absolute secret, as others would exploit or kill the young dragon for it.

event_ch22_assassins_in_the_dorm.title: Midnight Defense
event_ch22_assassins_in_the_dorm.guidance: Violet kills an assassin in her room using her daggers, realizing that some of her classmates are bypassing the rules to eliminate her.

event_ch23_dain_intrusion.title: The Mind Reader
event_ch23_dain_intrusion.guidance: Dain touches Violet's face to comfort her, but she pulls away, suddenly paranoid about what memories he might be pulling from her.

event_ch24_shattering_the_yard.title: The Sky Opens
event_ch24_shattering_the_yard.guidance: In a moment of sheer fury during a confrontation, Violet summons a massive bolt of lightning that splits the stone floor of the flight field.

event_ch25_imogen_training.title: Imogen's Help
event_ch25_imogen_training.guidance: Imogen secretly helps Violet train her physical stamina, revealing a softer side and a shared interest in keeping Violet alive.

event_ch26_the_rebel_weapons.title: Smuggled Steel
event_ch26_the_rebel_weapons.guidance: Violet observes Xaden packing boxes of alloy daggers capable of killing venin, realizing the rebellion is still very much active.

event_ch27_the_map_room.title: Scribe's Sight
event_ch27_the_map_room.guidance: Violet sneaks into the map room, cross-referencing military reports with actual border skirmish locations to find massive discrepancies.

event_ch28_academic_clash.title: The Scribe's Choice
event_ch28_academic_clash.guidance: Violet confronts her former scribe mentor, realizing how deeply the scribes are involved in censoring the horrors of the outside world.

event_ch29_the_storm_kiss.title: Rain and Lightning
event_ch29_the_storm_kiss.guidance: Xaden and Violet's confrontation about trust and loyalty turns into a passionate kiss in his quarters, breaking their professional boundaries.

event_ch30_the_memory_theft.title: The Realization of Betrayal
event_ch30_the_memory_theft.guidance: Violet pieces together that Dain stole the memory of Athebyne from her mind during a simple touch, exposing their plans to leadership.

event_ch31_the_march_out.title: Marching into the Trap
event_ch31_the_march_out.guidance: Violet's squad flies out under heavy rain, the atmosphere thick with foreboding as she realizes they are flying into a trap set by her own mother.

event_ch32_the_dead_post.title: The Ghost Town
event_ch32_the_dead_post.guidance: The squad explores the abandoned stone towers of Athebyne, finding no military presence but plenty of evidence of a hasty evacuation.

event_ch33_the_gryphon_arrival.title: Feathers in the Wind
event_ch33_the_gryphon_arrival.guidance: Three massive griffin flyers land on the battlements, their riders demanding the weapons Xaden promised to help defend their villages.

event_ch34_the_veil_lifted.title: The True Lore
event_ch34_the_veil_lifted.guidance: Xaden explains that the venin are draining the earth of magic to fuel their wyvern, and the wards of Navarre are the only things keeping them out.

event_ch35_the_sky_darkens.title: The Shadow of Wyvern
event_ch35_the_sky_darkens.guidance: The horizon fills with the flapping wings of wyvern, their riders channeling blue fire as they descend upon the defenseless village of Resson.

event_ch36_the_lightning_strike.title: Striking the Beast
event_ch36_the_lightning_strike.guidance: Violet channels her lightning signet directly into a wyvern's heart, vaporizing the beast and its venin rider in a massive explosion.

event_ch37_the_shadow_blade.title: The Black Blade
event_ch37_the_shadow_blade.guidance: A venin stabs Violet with a poisoned blade; she feels her strength drain instantly as the dark magic begins to rot her veins.

event_ch38_the_healing_sleep.title: The Mender's Touch
event_ch38_the_healing_sleep.guidance: Violet experiences fever dreams of her father and the archives before waking up to the sight of a beautiful, hidden mountain valley.

event_ch39_brennans_embrace.title: The Brother's Ghost
event_ch39_brennans_embrace.guidance: Brennan Sorrengail steps forward, his hand glowing with mending magic, welcoming Violet to the true revolution.

campaign.deathInstructions: If Violet is defeated or fails a lethal trial, she does not permanently die. Instead, she suffers a severe physical injury (such as a dislocated joint or a broken bone) that imposes a permanent physical penalty on her future rolls, or her dragons must sacrifice a portion of their own energy to shield her, straining her bond and increasing the difficulty of channeling her signet.

endGameRules.win: Violet successfully survives the Battle of Resson, uncovers the truth about the venin, reunites with her brother Brennan in Aretia, and commits herself to the secret revolution alongside Xaden.
endGameRules.lose: Violet is captured by Navarre's leadership or killed by the venin during the battle of Resson, leaving the secrets of the revolution buried and her dragons unbonded once more.
endGameRules.neutral: Violet survives the trials and the battle but is forced to flee into hiding alone, distrustful of both the corrupt Navarre military and Xaden's rebels, becoming a rogue rider in the borderlands.

With the wards beginning to fail and the truth leaking to the edges of the kingdom, the college has become a pressure cooker of political tension, lethal training, and forbidden knowledge.
Genre & Tone: Dark Military Fantasy, High-Stakes, Romance, and Grim Realism
Core Regional Conflict: The brutal, high-mortality training at Basgiath War College, set against Navarre's desperate, secret war against the venin and their wyvern forces, while the leadership actively censors the truth from its own citizens.

<nar>
The stone corridors of the military wing at {{Basgiath War College|loc}} are drafty, smelling of cold slate, dried ink, and the distant, sulfurous tang of dragonfire drifting from the high peaks. 

Violet Sorrengail shifted the heavy canvas satchel on her shoulder, the thick canvas strap cutting mercilessly into her collarbone. 
Inside, the weight of her life—carefully preserved historical scrolls, reference books on military tactics, and her late father's personal journals—clinked softly. 
Her knee gave a tiny, warning pop as she adjusted her weight, a familiar, dull ache blooming in her left joint. 
She ignored it, drawing a slow breath through her nose, steadying her pulse.

She had spent her entire nineteen years preparing for the quiet sanctuary of the {{Scribes Quadrant|faction}}. 
She knew the archives. 
She knew the smell of old vellum and the peaceful, rhythmic scratch of quills. 
But today was Conscription Day, and instead of entering the quiet halls of the historians, she had been summoned to the high tower office of the General.

Her mother.

As Violet approached the heavy oak door adorned with the double-headed dragon crest of Navarre, she realized it wasn't fully closed. 
A thin sliver of warm candlelight sliced through the gap, carrying with it the sharp, heated cadence of a voice she knew instantly.

"She will not survive the first week, Mother! Look at her! Her bones are like glass. The first run on the turret will snap her ankle, and if she even makes it to the Parapet, the wind will blow her off the edge!"

That was {{Mira Sorrengail|npc}}. 
Her older sister's voice was ragged with a rare, desperate panic. 

"She is a Sorrengail,"
their mother's voice cut through the air, smooth and hard as polished obsidian. 
{{General Lilith Sorrengail|npc}} did not raise her voice; she never had to. 
"A Sorrengail does not hide in the dust of the archives while her siblings bleed for the kingdom. Brennan gave his life. Mira, you have earned your spurs. Violet will enter the {{Riders Quadrant|faction}}, or she will die trying. I will not have a coward for a daughter."

Violet froze in the hallway, her fingers tightening around the strap of her satchel until her knuckles turned a stark, bloodless white. 
The betrayal was a physical blow, cold and sharp, settling deep into her chest. 
She had no choice. 
The mandate had been signed in her mother's unyielding black ink.

Through the high arched windows of the corridor, she could look down upon the conscription grounds below. 
A sea of hundreds of hopeful cadets, dressed in various states of leather armor and heavy boots, milled about the courtyard. 
Some looked terrified, clutching family heirlooms. 
Others paced like caged animals, their eyes scanning the high stone walls of the fortress with a desperate, hungry ambition. 

They were strong. 
They were whole. 
And she was standing there with protective linen wraps beneath her tunic just to keep her shoulders from slipping out of their sockets.

But as Violet looked down at the courtyard, her analytical mind began to catalog the details. 
She noticed the slight wear on the boots of the peasants from the southern provinces, the rigid, arrogant postures of the officers' children, and the nervous sweat glistening on the necks of those who wouldn't survive the first drop. 
She might be fragile, but she was not stupid. 
If she was going to be forced into the meat grinder of the riders, she would have to use every scrap of history, strategy, and observation her father had ever taught her to stay alive.

She let go of her satchel strap, smoothed down the front of her simple scribe's tunic, and pushed the heavy oak door open.

'Let them see me look.'
she thought, her jaw setting in that quiet, stubborn line her father always recognized. 
'Let them see exactly what they are trying to break.'
</nar>

Violet froze in the hallway, her fingers tightening around the strap of her satchel until her knuckles turned a stark, bloodless white. 
The betrayal was a physical blow, cold and sharp, settling deep into her chest. 
She had no choice. 
The mandate had been signed in her mother's unyielding black ink.

Through the high arched windows of the corridor, she could look down upon the conscription grounds below. 
A sea of hundreds of hopeful cadets, dressed in various states of leather armor and heavy boots, milled about the courtyard. 
Some looked terrified, clutching family heirlooms. 
Others paced like caged animals, their eyes scanning the high stone walls of the fortress with a desperate, hungry ambition. 

They were strong. 
They were whole. 
And she was standing there with protective linen wraps beneath her tunic just to keep her shoulders from slipping out of their sockets.

She noticed the slight wear on the boots of the peasants from the southern provinces, the rigid, arrogant postures of the officers' children, and the nervous sweat glistening on the necks of those who wouldn't survive the first drop. 
She might be fragile, but she was not stupid. 
If she was going to be forced into the meat grinder of the riders, she would have to use every scrap of history, strategy, and observation her father had ever taught her to stay alive.

She let go of her satchel strap, smoothed down the front of her simple scribe's tunic, and pushed the heavy oak door open.

twist: Mira doesn't offer comforting reassurances or sugarcoat the danger; instead, she coldly forces Violet to look at a cadet who has already fallen or been turned away, grounding the horror of the parapet in immediate, unyielding reality.

<nar>
The courtyard of Basgiath War College heaves with the nervous, adrenaline-soaked energy of hundreds of conscripts, the air sharp with the scent of wet wool, damp earth, and the raw, metallic tang of fear. 

{{Violet Sorrengail}} weaves through the press of armored bodies, her slight frame slipping past broad-shouldered candidates who already look like they were carved from granite. 

She spots her sister near the western archway, standing apart from the milling masses with the unmistakable, lethal ease of a second-year rider who has survived a year of bloodshed.

{{Mira Sorrengail|npc}} leans against a damp stone pillar, her leather riding leathers scuffed and travel-stained, her dark hair pulled back into a tight, utilitarian braid that emphasizes the hard angles of her jaw. 

When Violet approaches and asks her question, the older sister’s gaze snaps down, instantly sharp, fierce, and entirely devoid of sisterly warmth. 

Mira reaches out with surprising speed, grabbing Violet by the elbow of her tunic and yanking her behind the shelter of a thick buttress, out of earshot of the patrolling squad leaders.

"You think Mother sent you here to die, Violet, and you're right," Mira whispers, her voice rough, stripped of any comforting platitudes as she leans in close enough that Violet can smell the stale coffee and cold wind on her breath. 

Her fingers dig hard into Violet's arm, trembling ever so slightly—a telltale sign of exhaustion and terror that Mira instantly tries to mask by tightening her grip.

"They don't teach you how to cross [[The Parapet|loc]] because there is no technique that saves a brittle bone when the wind hits fifty knots," Mira continues, her eyes scanning the churning grey clouds above the citadel with bitter contempt. 

"What I’m not telling you is that the stone is slick with grease before dawn, that forty percent of our squad didn't make it across last year, and that if you freeze up halfway across, no one is turning back for you. Not Dain. Not the wingleaders. No one."

She drops her hand, stepping back slightly to let her gaze rake over Violet's delicate stature, lingering for a fraction of a second on the protective leather bindings wrapped carefully around Violet's fragile wrists and joints. 

"If you fall, I won't be able to catch you from the valley floor," Mira says, her voice dropping to a harsh, resonant undertone that brooks no argument. 

"So listen to me, and listen well: don't look down at the drop, keep your center of gravity low, and if your hips decide to slip out of their sockets halfway across, you damn well force them back into place with sheer spite. Am I understood?"

Before Violet can formulate a reply, the heavy bronze war-gongs of the citadel begin to toll, echoing across the basalt courtyard and signaling the mandatory assembly for the lethal trials ahead. 

Cadets around them stiffen, breaking off conversations as the iron-shod boots of the leadership march toward the staging grounds, drawing every eye upward toward the narrow, mist-shrouded stone bridge that spans the dizzying chasm.
</nar>

<plan>
twist: Instead of finding a weapon or a protective charm, the object from her books is a piece of home—a private, contraband historical letter that changes her understanding of the very fortress she's standing in.
distinct: Violet reacts not with shock at the magic of the moment, but with immediate, tactical paranoia, quickly concealing the parchment against her ribs before anyone—especially Dain or an eagle-eyed squad leader—catches sight of the forbidden script.

<nar>
The heavy parchment slips free from the reinforced spine of an old military history compendium just as {{Violet Sorrengail}} adjusts her leather shoulder bindings. 

It flutters down against the damp cobblestones of {{The Parapet|loc}}, catching the howling morning wind before Violet lunges forward with a sharp, synchronized gasp, pinning it beneath her palm against her thigh.

Her heart hammers against her ribs as she glances around in a panic. 

Around her, cadets are buckling helms and checking daggers, too absorbed in their own terror to notice a fluttering page, but the cold weight of the discovery settles heavily in her stomach. 

She pulls the folded paper close to her chest, her fingers trembling slightly as she slides it inside the inner pocket of her tunic, right against the protective leather wrapping of her ribs.

When she steals a glance at the paper's edge, she recognizes the sharp, meticulous ink strokes immediately. 

It is her late father’s handwriting—unmistakable, precise, and entirely forbidden by the edicts of {{Navarre Military Leadership|faction}}.

'They are hiding the rot at the edges, Violet,' the first visible line whispers from the dark ink, etched into her memory before she folds it tighter. 

'The wards are failing not because of weather, but because the source is being starved. If you are reading this in the Quadrant, your mother has condemned you to the front lines to silence what we discovered in the archives.'

The cold realization strikes harder than the mountain wind howling across the chasm. 

Her father hadn't just studied history; he had mapped its fractures, leaving her a compass built of truths that the {{Scribes Quadrant|loc}} would execute her for possessing.

Footsteps crunch heavily on the gravel nearby, and {{Dain Aetos|npc}} steps into her field of vision, his protective armor gleaming with polish and his jaw set in a hard, uncompromising line of childhood familiarity and sudden, overbearing authority.

"Violet," Dain calls out, his voice cutting through the rising gale as he stops before her, his eyes scanning her fragile frame with an expression that mixes deep affection with abrasive disapproval. 

"You shouldn't even be holding a book out here today, let alone carrying papers from the archives. The first detachment is moving out to {{The Parapet|loc}} in two minutes. Pull your leathers tighter and stay directly behind me on the stone. I'll make sure you don't fall."
</nar>

The breath catches in {{Violet Sorrengail}}’s throat, a cold, sharp pinch of winter air that she forces down into her lungs with absolute, deliberate control. 

She tucks her father’s folded letter deeper into her tunic, her fingers curling into tight fists inside her leather bracers to steady the tremor in her hands. 

Around her, the murmurs of the courtyard fade into the deafening roar of the mountain wind slamming against the sheer basalt cliffs of {{The Parapet|loc}}.

"Violet, wait—don't be an idiot," {{Dain Aetos|npc}} snaps, his hand shooting out to catch her by the shoulder, his grip heavy, familiar, and suffocatingly protective. 

"You can't do this. I told your mother I’d watch out for you, and I won't let you throw your life away on a stunt. Step back in line with the Scribes."

Violet doesn't flinch, though the pressure of his hand sends a dull, familiar ache radiating through her collarbone. 

She turns her head slowly, fixing Dain with a gaze as hard and unyielding as flint, her voice dropping into a quiet, icy cadence that brooks no debate.

"Remove your hand, Dain," she says, her tone slicing through the gale with crystalline precision. 

"If [[General Lilith Sorrengail|npc]] wants me dead, she'll have to watch me walk across that stone on my own two feet. I am not hiding in the archives."

Dain’s jaw tightens, his hazel eyes flashing with a mix of disbelief, anger, and helpless frustration as he slowly drops his hand, realizing too late that his overbearing interference only stokes her stubborn fire. 

He steps back, shaking his head in silent condemnation just as the squad leader at the head of the formation bellows the order to advance.

Violet squares her shoulders, ignoring the speculative, mocking stares of the armored cadets pressing in around her. 

She steps past Dain, her boots meeting the ancient, frost-slicked stone of [[The Parapet|loc]] for the very first time. 

The wind hits her instantly, a roaring, invisible wall of force that threatens to sweep her off balance before she has even taken a second step. 

Below her, the sheer drop into the mist-choked valley yawns wide, an abyss of jagged grey rock and whistling emptiness that demands absolute perfection from every step.
</nar>
